proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5a-5c of the parent proof. These are the pointwise error-term and main-term estimates on Bbar_r(0) with Q = Dzeta. Here they are stated for a general set K with explicit bounds. The supremum s_k of step 5b is replaced by the equivalent epsilon form of uniform convergence. Uniform convergence of maps F_k : R^n -> R to F on K means: for every eps > 0 there is k0 such that |F(z) - F_k(z)| < eps for all k >= k0 and all z in K (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff). The same holds for L-valued maps, with the operator norm.
1. Nonnegative constants. Put r0 := max(r, 0), Z0 := max(Z, 0) and N0 := max(N, 0); all three are >= 0. Let z be in K. Then 0 <= |z| <= r <= r0. Since t -> t^alpha is monotone on [0, infinity) for alpha >= 0 (Real.rpow_le_rpow), |z|^alpha <= r0^alpha. Also |z|^alpha >= 0 and r0^alpha >= 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg). Finally ||Q(z)|| <= Z <= Z0 and ||V(z)|| <= N <= N0. Using r0, Z0 and N0 avoids a case split when K is empty.
2. Bilinear bound. Let C_A := ||A||, the operator norm of A as a continuous linear map L -> L*. Then C_A >= 0 and |A[P][P']| <= C_A ||P|| ||P'|| for all P, P' in L (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm₂; the norm on R is the absolute value). Lean note: to synthesize the norm on the bilinear-form type, put `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3 in` before the theorem. The statement itself does not mention ||A||.
3. Claim (i): choice of k0. Fix eps > 0. Put C1 := (1 + r0^alpha)(N0 + 1) Z0 and C2 := C_A Z0; both are >= 0. Three facts hold for all sufficiently large k:
 a. |c_k| < (eps/2)/(C1 + 1), since c_k -> 0;
 b. ||U_k(z) - V(z)|| < min(1, (eps/2)/(C2 + 1)) for all z in K, since U_k -> V uniformly on K;
 c. the coefficient bound holds for every z in K, by hypothesis.
 Choose k0 such that a, b and c hold for every k >= k0.
4. Fix k >= k0 and z in K. Write P := U_k(z) and Q' := Q(z). By 3b, ||P - V(z)|| < 1, so ||P|| <= ||V(z)|| + ||P - V(z)|| <= N0 + 1.
5. Decomposition. A is linear in its first argument, so A[P][Q'] - A[V(z)][Q'] = A[P - V(z)][Q'] (map_sub, then evaluation of a difference of linear forms at Q'). Hence A[V(z)][Q'] - ah_k(z)[P][Q'] = -((ah_k(z)[P][Q'] - A[P][Q']) + A[P - V(z)][Q']).
6. First term. The coefficient bound gives |ah_k(z)[P][Q'] - A[P][Q']| <= c_k (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||Q'||. The factors 1 + |z|^alpha, ||P|| and ||Q'|| are >= 0, so this is <= |c_k| (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||Q'||. By steps 1 and 4 that is <= |c_k| (1 + r0^alpha)(N0 + 1) Z0 = |c_k| C1. By 3a, |c_k| C1 <= (eps/2) C1/(C1 + 1) < eps/2.
7. Second term. By step 2, |A[P - V(z)][Q']| <= C_A ||P - V(z)|| ||Q'|| <= C_A ||P - V(z)|| Z0 = ||P - V(z)|| C2. By 3b this is <= (eps/2) C2/(C2 + 1) < eps/2.
8. Steps 5 to 7 and the triangle inequality give |A[V(z)][Q(z)] - ah_k(z)[U_k(z)][Q(z)]| < eps/2 + eps/2 = eps for every k >= k0 and every z in K. Since eps > 0 was arbitrary, claim (i) holds.
9. Claim (ii). Fix eps > 0 and put C3 := r0^alpha Z0 >= 0. Since d_k -> 0 and the bound on Psi_k holds eventually, there is k1 such that every k >= k1 satisfies |d_k| < eps/(C3 + 1) and |Psi_k(z)[P]| <= d_k |z|^alpha ||P|| for all z in K and P in L. For such k and z in K, step 1 gives |0 - Psi_k(z)[Q(z)]| = |Psi_k(z)[Q(z)]| <= d_k |z|^alpha ||Q(z)|| <= |d_k| |z|^alpha ||Q(z)|| <= |d_k| r0^alpha Z0 = |d_k| C3 <= eps C3/(C3 + 1) < eps. Hence z -> Psi_k(z)[Q(z)] converges to 0 uniformly on K. QED.
key_steps: nonnegative constants r0, Z0, N0 with |z|^alpha <= r0^alpha, ||Q(z)|| <= Z0, ||V(z)|| <= N0 on K, and C_A = ||A|| with |A[P][P']| <= C_A ||P|| ||P'||
given eps > 0, eventually |c_k| < (eps/2)/(C1+1), ||U_k - V|| < min(1, (eps/2)/(C2+1)) on K, and the coefficient bound holds on K
A[V][Q] - ah_k[U_k][Q] = -((ah_k - A)[U_k][Q] + A[U_k - V][Q]), with ||U_k|| <= N0 + 1
each of the two terms is < eps/2, so the pairings converge uniformly on K
|Psi_k(z)[Q(z)]| <= |d_k| r0^alpha Z0 < eps eventually, so the error forms converge uniformly to 0 on K
